references.observation: The restored front view shows a high tapering tail, open passage, irregular clay flanks and the hollow flower at the right. The two piers flare around the ground and each has a deep asymmetric hollow below a projecting lip.

references.credit: Adunni Olorisha Trust / Adunni Osun Foundation
references.observation: The entrance side shows the wider stair and adjoining sculpted walls, including the tall open ornament beside the flower.

references.credit: Adunni Olorisha Trust / Adunni Osun Foundation
references.observation: The courtyard view shows a flared rear shoulder, splayed feet, the open threshold and the adjoining wall profile. One lower hollow faces the courtyard near the root, while the opposite hollow sits higher on the pier.
The Trust records the 2011 restoration, identifies the sculptors and links the gate to the Sacred Potter Field.
The rear view shows the larger hollow flower at left, the gate’s opening and a person crossing onto the paved road. The geotag gives the camera station.

map.note: The geotagged rear photo shows the paved access road directly through the arch, with the larger flower wall on the left. The photograph places the gate west of the mapped road. The preview uses the road station nearest the tagged camera and faces across the road at 93° true. The 8.1 m setback from the PMTiles centerline follows the visible approach and modeled steps. The GPS tag is a camera position, and the exact threshold position and facing are estimated.

route.note: The photographer’s tag and GPS sample are consistent. Both are records from the same visit.

limitations: The source depicts the restored entrance and the nearest flower walls. The complete enclosure, exact dimensions and small sculpture details remain unverified.
The 2013 photo identifies the roadside and outward side. The threshold setback, bearing and ground elevations are interpreted from that photograph, PMTiles and terrain samples.
